history.summary: NON-TEMPLE / ARCHAEOLOGICAL MONUMENT FLAG: the famous Bhitargaon temple is NOT a functioning temple - it is a 5th-century Gupta-era brick monument protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. It is the earliest surviving brick/terracotta Hindu shrine with a roof and a tall pyramidal shikhara; built of large bricks and fronted with terracotta panels depicting Shiva, Vishnu, aquatic monsters and scenes of daily life and mythology. Square plan with double-recessed corners, faces east; its entrance shows one of the first uses of the semi-circular doorway that Alexander Cunningham (first ASI Director-General, 1871) called the 'Hindu arch'. The upper chamber was damaged (lightning in the 19th century per one source; 18th century per another - verify). Documented and protected by the ASI. CSV TOWN FLAG: actual town is Bhitargaon (Ghatampur area), about 35 km from Kanpur city - not Kanpur.

name: Bhitargaon Temple

town_description: Bhitargaon is a village in the Ghatampur area of Kanpur Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh, roughly 35 km from Kanpur city. Its name is inseparable from the Gupta-era brick temple - the greatest surviving Indian brick temple of the Gupta Empire - which draws archaeology and architecture enthusiasts rather than worshippers.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavite, historically) - now an ASI-protected archaeological monument, not a functioning temple
